question.nlq: Could you tell me the top 5 school districts with the highest average FRPM eligibility percentage for K-12 in the 2014-2015 academic year among schools that have SAT math scores above the state average, along with the number of charter schools in each of those districts?

meanings.gt_sql:
WITH state_avg_math AS (
    SELECT AVG(AvgScrMath) AS avg_math
    FROM satscores
    WHERE AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL
),
filtered_schools AS (
    SELECT f."District Name",
           f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)",
           f."Charter School (Y/N)"
    FROM frpm f
    JOIN satscores s ON f.CDSCode = s.cds
    WHERE f."Academic Year" = '2014-2015'
      AND s.AvgScrMath > (SELECT avg_math FROM state_avg_math)
)
SELECT
    "District Name" AS district_name,
    AVG("Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)") AS average_frpm_eligible_percent,
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Charter School (Y/N)" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS charter_school_count
FROM filtered_schools
GROUP BY "District Name"
ORDER BY average_frpm_eligible_percent DESC
LIMIT 5;

turns.sql:
WITH state_avg AS (SELECT AVG(AvgScrMath) AS avg_math FROM satscores WHERE AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL),
eligible_schools AS (
  SELECT s.District,
         f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS frpm_pct,
       CASE WHEN f."Charter School (Y/N)" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_charter
  FROM frpm f
  JOIN schools s ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode
  JOIN satscores sc ON f.CDSCode = sc.cds
  JOIN state_avg sa ON 1=1
  WHERE f."Academic Year" = '2014-2015'
    AND sc.AvgScrMath IS NOT NULL
    AND sc.AvgScrMath > sa.avg_math
)
SELECT District,
       AVG(frpm_pct) AS avg_frpm_eligibility_pct,
       SUM(is_charter) AS charter_school_count
FROM eligible_schools
GROUP BY District
ORDER BY avg_frpm_eligibility_pct DESC
LIMIT 5;
